data.name: Guide_Intro
data.value: Everything Hotline does, in short. Each part says where in Settings to change it.

data.name: Guide_Open_Body
data.value: Press the Copilot key to open or close the panel; hold it to start a new chat. Settings › General changes what a press and a hold do (a hold can also be voice input) and adds an extra shortcut. The panel opens on the monitor you're working on, ready to type. Esc or clicking elsewhere closes it, unless it's pinned.

data.name: Guide_Connections_Body
data.value: Pick the effort, model and provider in the button row. Settings › AI connections adds them: Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity installed on this PC (they use their own sign-in), an API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible) or a local model server. Test checks a key and model.

data.name: Guide_Attach_Body
data.value: The + button attaches files, the window you were in, the whole screen or a region you drag out. You can also paste or drop images and files. Text you had selected in the app you came from comes along by itself. Models that can't see images get the text in the screenshot instead.

data.name: Guide_Voice_Body
data.value: Set the long press to Voice input (Settings › General), hold the key and talk; let go to stop. Settings › Chat and history decides whether it sends right away.

data.name: Guide_Actions_Body
data.value: Type / for /translate, /summarize, /fix, /explain or your own (Settings › Quick actions). The document button picks the system prompt (Settings › Prompts).

data.name: Guide_Memory_Body
data.value: /remember and a note saves it for every chat, whichever AI you use. Settings › Chat and history opens memory.md to edit it.

data.name: Guide_History_Body
data.value: The clock button, Ctrl+Up in an empty message box, or /resume opens your chats; type to search. A chat with Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity lives in that tool's own history and picks up where it left off. Continue in (in the list, or its button) opens it in a terminal; the other tools are under More….

data.name: Guide_Background_Body
data.value: Ask something long and switch away: a Windows notification says when it's ready. Esc stops an answer; while the AI is thinking, the cursor spins.

data.name: Guide_Move_Body
data.value: Hold Alt: drag the grip on the message bar's edge to move the panel, or a side to resize it. Right-click the grip to save the spot and size as the default, or to go back to it. A moved panel opens at its default the next time, unless it's pinned (the pin button): then it stays where you put it until you unpin it, click into another app or restart Hotline.

data.name: Guide_Direction_Body
data.value: The chat grows from the message bar: up, unless there's no room above, then down. Settings › Window can keep it up or down and sets the position, width and chat height.

data.name: Guide_Rows_Body
data.value: Settings › Window › Button rows shows the bar as six areas: left, center and right of the row above the message box, and the same three below it. Drag a button or a picker to move it inside an area or to another one, or use its arrow buttons (Alt+arrow changes area, Ctrl+arrow changes the order). What you hide waits in “Not shown”. Every button can have its own size, an outline or a fill, and you can add buttons of your own that run a quick action or insert a text. Buttons that don't fit move into a ⋯ menu.

data.name: Guide_Sounds_Body
data.value: Settings › Appearance › Sounds plays a sound when the panel opens or closes: a Windows sound or a .wav in your sounds folder. Off by default.

data.name: Guide_Files_Body
data.value: Everything is in your .hotline folder and applies as you save: settings.json, one file per connection, prompts, quick actions and toolbar.json. Replace a file to switch setups; Settings › Advanced › Reset starts over, with a backup. API keys are kept in Windows Credential Locker, never in a file.

data.name: Bar_SizeLimitNote
data.value: Custom buttons are limited to 80 × 80 DIP; larger sizes stop there.

data.name: Bar_EditorIntro
data.value: Drag items between the four groups, or use the buttons under each item. With an item focused, Alt+arrow keys move it to another group and Ctrl+Left or Ctrl+Right move it within its group. Changes are saved to toolbar.json and applied at once.
